nominal_profiles: neuter external referent to which a jackal is dear

rules.masculine_strong: 7.1.95 compares the form of the same-root tṛj derivative in non-vocative sarvanāmasthāna. Masculine has kroṣṭā but vocative singular kroṣṭo. Accusative plural kroṣṭūn stays outside this strong set.
rules.masculine_oblique: 7.1.97 optionally extends the comparison at vowel-initial endings from the instrumental onward. A consonant-initial bhis does not meet that condition. The source specifically gives kroṣṭubhiḥ.
rules.neuter_oblique: 7.1.73–74, with the priority note in 7.1.97 and the Kaumudī examples at 7.1.75. On ordinary neuter treatment num supplies priyakroṣṭune. Under Gālava’s optional masculine-like treatment the independent u/tṛj choice gives priyakroṣṭave and priyakroṣṭre. Instrumental has only two distinct spellings because the ordinary neuter num route and an allowed masculine treatment give the same priyakroṣṭunā.
rules.accent: Under the specifically feminine route of 7.1.96, the source explains kroṣṭrī with final udātta under 6.1.174 even on the ṅīp analysis. The present unaccented tables carry no new historical Vedic attestations.
